lines.text: It is project time! Today you build a drawing studio where the user is the artist.
Give every shape its own function: draw_square(size), draw_star(size) and so on.
Each one is short and easy to test.
The main program just picks which one to call.
Ask the user for a shape, a colour and a size.
Clean the shape with .strip().lower() and turn the size into a number with int().
Then if, elif and else call the right function.
A while loop keeps the studio open.
Each time round it asks for a new shape.
When the user types done, set the loop variable to False and the studio closes.
Shapes on top of each other look messy.
A move_to_spot(number) function can lift the pen, goto a new place and put the pen down.
Then every shape gets its own space.
Each shape gets its own small function with a size parameter.
A star turns one hundred and forty-four degrees five times, and goes round the centre twice.
The user typed Star with a capital letter, and lower turns it into star.
The if and elif lines choose which shape function to call, with the size the user chose.
The while loop keeps asking for shapes while drawing is True.
Typing done switches drawing to False, so the loop ends and the studio closes.
Build one shape function, test it, and only then add the next.
When the menu works, wrap it in a loop and let a friend become the artist.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now plan it, build it, test it, and share it!
